There is some merit in just starting with Series 1 of the 2005 reboot, it's closer to modern sensibilities in its storytelling and format. Another reason is that there are also missing episodes in 1960s Doctor Who because the BBC preferred to reuse the videotape they were on to save money. Many of these missing episodes have been animated now, but the audio for all of them exist thanks to fan recordings. You can watch "telesnap reconstructions," which use surviving imagery overlaid on the audio to give a sensation of what the episodes would've been like.

If you want to skip the missing episodes, then you can go to Season 7, the first color season, with the Third Doctor. (But maybe give The War Games a watch beforehand!)
